slice: Sparse-view / few-shot Gaussian splatting (~10-30 camera stations): InstantSplat lineage, depth-prior regularization, 2025-2026 few-shot 3DGS papers, and the 360-photo-to-cubemap angle
summary: Sparse-view 3DGS has moved fast over the last year along two axes relevant to a 20-station bridge shoot. First, pose/init: classical COLMAP struggles when only ~20 widely-spaced stations exist, so the field has shifted to feed-forward pointmap networks (DUSt3R -> MASt3R -> VGGT -> pi3) that jointly predict poses+depth+points and explicitly target "sparse and low-overlap" capture — exactly this use case; VGGT's code became commercial-use-friendly (excluding military) on 2025-07-29. Second, regularization: since InstantSplat (2024) established DUSt3R-init plus fast optimization for sparse views, a wave of 2025-2026 papers (FSGS, DNGaussian, CoR-GS, SparseGS, MS-GS, Pi-GS, DropAnSH-GS, SaveWildGS) converged on a shared recipe — monocular-depth-prior losses (Pearson correlation, not raw L2), pseudo/virtual-view interpolation between real cameras, and anchor-cluster or spherical-harmonic-coefficient dropout — to fight the two dominant failure modes: near-camera floaters and view-overfitting, rather than relying on plain opacity-reset. Pi-GS (Feb 2026) beats InstantSplat/FSGS/DNGaussian on Tanks&Temples 3-view and also reports MipNeRF360 12/24-view outdoor results. A separate but directly relevant line handles 360/panoramic captures natively: ODGS and Splatter-360 do spherical-domain (cubemap or ERP) rasterization instead of independent perspective crops, and PanoImager/LighthouseGS explicitly flag that sparse panoramic stations degrade cross-view consistency and extrapolation. No paper tests exactly "20 outdoor bridge panoramas," but MS-GS and SaveWildGS (in-the-wild, distractors, appearance variation across sessions) and Seam360GS (dual-fisheye seam/distortion calibration) each match a specific real-world hazard this shoot will hit: traffic/pedestrian ghosting, lighting drift between stations, and stitching seams. A practical (non-peer-reviewed) blog independently converged on splitting each 360 frame into 18 perspective views (a ring of 16 plus 2 poles) rather than a plain 6-face cubemap, precisely to answer the "many perspective views per panorama" question.

sources.title: InstantSplat: Sparse-view Gaussian Splatting in Seconds
key_claims: Self-supervised framework unprojects 2D pixels into 3D using DUSt3R geometric priors and eliminates Structure-from-Motion entirely.
Reconstruction is >30x faster than SfM+3DGS and improves SSIM from 0.3755 to 0.7624 on sparse-view benchmarks.
Official repo (NVlabs/InstantSplat) supports 3D-GS, 2D-GS, and Mip-Splatting; 33 commits, README does not pin an exact minimum view count.
quotes: Unbounded Sparse-view Pose-free Gaussian Splatting in 40 Seconds

sources.title: FSGS: Real-Time Few-shot View Synthesis using Gaussian Splatting
key_claims: Works with as few as 3 training views using a Gaussian Unpooling process that adds new Gaussians near representative locations to infill vacant areas.
Benchmarked on both indoor (LLFF) and outdoor unbounded (Mip-NeRF360) scenes plus Blender.

sources.title: CoR-GS: Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting via Co-regularization
key_claims: Trains dual Gaussian radiance fields simultaneously and uses co-pruning plus co-regularization between the two fields to improve accuracy of Gaussian primitives under sparse views.

sources.title: Pi-GS: Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with Dense π3 Initialization
key_claims: Uses π3, a reference-free point-cloud estimation network, for dense initialization instead of COLMAP, combined with confidence-aware Pearson-correlation depth loss, normal-consistency loss, and depth-warped pseudo-views generated by circle interpolation between camera pairs.
On Tanks&Temples 3-view PSNR: Pi-GS 22.87 vs Intern-GS 22.67, FSGS 22.31, InstantSplat 22.20, DNGaussian 20.69.
Also evaluated at 12-view and 24-view settings on MipNeRF360 (real outdoor 360-degree scenes).
Code public at github.com/Mango0000/Pi-GS.

sources.title: Dropping Anchor and Spherical Harmonics for Sparse-view Gaussian Splatting (DropAnSH-GS)
key_claims: Accepted CVPR 2026; identifies that prior random-Gaussian dropout regularizers suffer a 'neighbor compensation effect' where dropped Gaussians get compensated by neighbors, weakening regularization.
Proposes anchor-based dropout that removes whole spatial neighbor clusters at once, plus dropping higher-degree spherical-harmonic coefficients to reduce color-based overfitting.
Official code at github.com/Fangkang515/DropAnSH-GS.

sources.title: MS-GS: Multi-Appearance Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild
key_claims: Targets in-the-wild photo collections with limited images taken at different times of day or seasons (multi-appearance), built on monocular-depth-estimation geometric priors.
Adds geometry-guided supervision at virtual (interpolated) views at both pixel and feature levels to reduce overfitting.
Accepted at NeurIPS 2025.

sources.title: Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild (SaveWildGS)
key_claims: Handles sparse (3/6/9-view) real-world outdoor landmark photos with transient distractors (people, vehicles) via a one-step diffusion reference-guided view refinement, sparsity-aware Gaussian replication (SAGR), and LoRA test-time training with score-distillation loss.
Reports 17.2% PSNR, 10.8% SSIM, 4.0% LPIPS improvement over prior sparse-view baselines on NeRF On-the-go and Photo Tourism (outdoor) plus LLFF.

Explicitly documents two failure modes: difficulty separating static distractors (parked cars, standing pedestrians) from real background, and that overlapped camera perspectives reduce available reference regions, degrading reconstruction.
quotes: overlapped camera perspectives reduce available reference regions

sources.title: ODGS: 3D Scene Reconstruction from Omnidirectional Images with 3D Gaussian Splattings
key_claims: Decomposes each omnidirectional (360) image into six perspective cubemap-face images and rasterizes them directly rather than warping a single equirectangular projection, avoiding the distortion a naive perspective rasterizer produces on 360 images.
Achieves 100x faster optimization/rendering than NeRF-based omnidirectional methods; evaluated on OmniBlender, Ricoh360, OmniPhotos, 360Roam, OmniScenes, 360VO.
Official repo (esw0116/ODGS) is MIT-licensed; last updated 2024-12-26.

sources.title: Splatter-360: Generalizable 360-degree Gaussian Splatting for Wide-baseline Panoramic Images
key_claims: Feed-forward 3DGS for wide-baseline panorama pairs; performs multi-view matching directly in the spherical domain via a spherical sweep algorithm building a spherical cost volume.

Uses a bi-projection encoder combining equirectangular projection (ERP) and cube-map projection features through multi-view transformers, addressing distortion that naive independent cubemap-face processing introduces.

sources.title: PanoImager: Geometry-Guided Novel View Synthesis and Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramic Views
key_claims: States directly that sparse panoramic observations 'can degrade geometric completeness, cross-view consistency, and extrapolation to unseen viewpoints' for sphere-native 3DGS extensions.
quotes: sparse observations can degrade geometric completeness, cross-view consistency, and extrapolation to unseen viewpoints

sources.title: LighthouseGS: Indoor Structure-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting for Panorama-Style Mobile Captures
key_claims: Targets exactly a 'panorama-style' multi-station capture pattern (indoor), i.e. a small number of 360-style stations rather than a dense video walkthrough — structurally the closest existing analog to a 20-station outdoor shoot, though scoped to indoor scenes.

sources.title: Seam360GS: Seamless 360-degree Gaussian Splatting from Real-World Omnidirectional Images
key_claims: Addresses lens-separation seams and angular distortion artifacts specific to consumer dual-fisheye 360 cameras (the Insta360 X4 Air's own capture hardware) by jointly optimizing a dual-fisheye camera calibration model together with the Gaussian parameters.
Licensed CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
key_claims: 1.2B-parameter feed-forward transformer that jointly predicts camera extrinsics/intrinsics, depth maps, point maps, and 3D point tracks in under one second, explicitly described as working 'even from sparse and low-overlap datasets.'

As of 2025-07-29 the repository code license was updated to permit commercial use excluding military applications; only the VGGT-1B-Commercial checkpoint is commercially licensed, the original checkpoint remains non-commercial, and a Hugging Face mirror is MIT-licensed.

InstantSplat-style pipelines use this class of model (DUSt3R/MASt3R/VGGT/pi3) in place of classical incremental SfM specifically because sparse, low-overlap station capture breaks COLMAP-style matching.
quotes: even from sparse and low-overlap datasets

sources.title: TIDI-GS: Floater Suppression in 3D Gaussian Splatting for Enhanced Indoor Scene Fidelity
key_claims: Combines a temporally accumulated evidence log, conservative detail-preserving guards, isolation-aware removal policy, and an uncertainty-guided monocular depth regularizer to suppress floaters without architecture changes.
Scoped and evaluated on indoor scenes; outdoor/unbounded transfer is not confirmed in the available abstract.

sources.title: I Built My Own Tools to Turn 360° Footage Into Clean Gaussian Splatting Data
key_claims: Practitioner tool (3DGaussianTools) projects each 360 frame onto 18 virtual perspective cameras — 16 in a ring (8 yaw angles x 2 pitch levels at +/-35 degrees) plus 2 polar (zenith/nadir) cameras — instead of a plain 6-face cubemap, specifically to avoid pole distortion and enable per-view object detection/segmentation.

Runs YOLO + SAM per perspective view to mask transient objects (people, selfie sticks), reprojects masks back to equirectangular space, and dilates masks ~15% to fully cover fringes (hair, shadow, motion blur) before training.
Exports either a COLMAP-style dataset (cropped cubemap faces) or a Nerfstudio-style transforms.json.

sources.title: Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction: Recent Advances and Open Challenges
key_claims: Survey covering explicit point-cloud-based approaches including 3D Gaussian Splatting, framing geometric regularization, explicit shape modeling, and generative inference as the three main strategies against floaters and pose ambiguities in sparse-view reconstruction.

recommendations: Swap (or augment) the pycolmap/COLMAP pose-estimation stage for a feed-forward pointmap network — VGGT or the lighter pi3/DUSt3R/MASt3R family — since these are explicitly built for the 'sparse and low-overlap' regime that 20 widely-spaced bridge stations will produce, where classical incremental SfM feature-matching is most likely to fail or drop stations.

When exploding each equirectangular JPG into perspective crops for reconstruction, use a ~18-view ring (e.g. 8 yaw angles x 2 pitch bands around +/-35 degrees, plus zenith/nadir) rather than a plain 6-face cubemap — this is the specific technique a practitioner (3DGaussianTools/realitystack blog) converged on for exactly this conversion, and it avoids the pole-distortion and low-parallax-density problems of a bare 6-face split.

Add a monocular-depth regularization loss (Pearson-correlation style against a pretrained depth model such as Depth Anything v2, as used in DNGaussian/MS-GS/Pi-GS) to the gsplat training loop — this is the single most consistently-reported fix across 2025-2026 few-shot 3DGS papers for the floater/overfitting failure mode that ~20 stations will trigger, and is a modest addition to an existing training loop rather than a new architecture.

Replace or supplement plain opacity-reset with an anchor/cluster-based Gaussian dropout regularizer (DropAnSH-GS) or utilization-based pruning during training — plain opacity reset is documented as weaker at cleaning outdoor floaters because dropped Gaussians get 'neighbor compensated' by nearby ones.

Plan for transient-object masking per perspective crop (traffic, pedestrians, parked vehicles) before photometric loss, mirroring the YOLO+SAM-then-dilate-then-reproject workflow in the practical blog and the distractor-handling in MS-GS/SaveWildGS — a bridge-and-roadway scene captured across ~20 separate stations is very likely to include moving vehicles in at least some frames.

If the 20 stations were shot at different times of day or in variable light (common for an outdoor multi-stop bridge survey), consider a lightweight per-image appearance embedding (MS-GS's approach) rather than assuming globally consistent exposure/white balance across stations.

Treat native panorama-domain training (ODGS-style cubemap rasterization or Splatter-360-style ERP+cubemap fusion) as a stretch goal, not a v1 requirement — it requires custom rasterizer work beyond Orbit Studio's current Spark/gsplat crop-based pipeline and should only be prototyped if the simpler perspective-crop-plus-depth-regularization approach plateaus in quality.

Budget extra floater-cleanup attention specifically for open sky and distant roadway/horizon regions — every sparse-view GS failure-mode discussion found (survey 2507.16406, TIDI-GS, DropAnSH-GS, SaveWildGS) names floaters and unbounded/far-background geometry as the primary artifact class, and a bridge-plus-roadway scene has exactly that kind of large-depth-range, sparsely-observed background.
uncertainties: The exact license terms of the NVlabs/InstantSplat repository were not confirmed beyond the presence of a LICENSE.txt file (likely a restrictive NVIDIA research license); verify before shipping it as part of an open pipeline.

Whether the 'Depth-Regularized Optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting in Few-Shot Images' paper (arXiv 2311.13398) is the same work commonly referred to as 'DNGaussian' or a separate paper with a similar title was not fully disambiguated from search results alone.
Whether TIDI-GS's floater-suppression technique (indoor-scoped per its title) transfers effectively to unbounded outdoor bridge/roadway scenes was not confirmed.

No paper or blog post was found that tests the precise combination in this task — roughly 20 outdoor 360-degree still panoramas of a bridge/roadway reconstructed via cubemap-split 3DGS; all recommendations are extrapolated from adjacent sparse-view, panoramic, and in-the-wild work rather than a single directly-matching source.

VRAM/runtime feasibility of running VGGT or pi3 (billion-parameter-class feed-forward networks) inside a free-tier Google Colab T4 (16GB) session, as Orbit Studio's pipeline currently relies on, was not confirmed from any source found; this should be tested directly before committing to it as a COLMAP replacement.
The realitystack Substack blog post is a practitioner account, not peer-reviewed, and its exact publication date could not be confirmed beyond internal references to YOLO26/SAM3.1 suggesting 2026.
